question: Under Nevada Administrative Code, how long must a real estate broker keep complete real estate transaction and property management records after the date of closing or the last activity involving the property?
choice_a: 2 years
choice_b: 5 years
choice_c: 3 years
choice_d: 7 years
explanation: NAC 645.650(1) requires a broker to keep complete real estate transaction and property management records for at least 5 years after the date of closing or the last activity involving the property, unless otherwise directed by the Division.

question: Nevada's 5-year record-retention requirement for brokers under NAC 645.650 explicitly extends to which of the following?
choice_a: Only completed transactions that closed escrow
choice_b: Only records involving a trust account deposit
choice_c: Offers that were not accepted and transactions that were not completed
choice_d: Only records the Division specifically requests in writing
explanation: NAC 645.650(1) states the 5-year retention duty applies to complete transaction and property management records 'including, without limitation, offers that were not accepted and transactions that were not completed.'

question: Under NAC 645.650(2), within how many calendar days after paperwork is executed by all parties must a salesperson or broker-salesperson provide that paperwork to the broker with whom he or she is associated?
choice_a: 1 day
choice_b: 3 days
choice_c: 10 days
choice_d: 5 calendar days
explanation: NAC 645.650(2) requires a salesperson or broker-salesperson to provide any paperwork to the broker within 5 calendar days after that paperwork is executed by all the parties, ensuring timely submission of records to the broker.

question: Under NRS 645.254, absent a court order or the client's written permission, for how long after the revocation or termination of a brokerage agreement must a licensee refrain from disclosing confidential information relating to the client?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 6 months
choice_c: 2 years
choice_d: Indefinitely
explanation: NRS 645.254(2) prohibits a licensee from disclosing confidential information relating to a client for 1 year after the revocation or termination of the brokerage agreement, unless required by court order or given written client permission.

question: When a broker assigns different licensees affiliated with the same brokerage to represent separate parties in the same real estate transaction under NRS 645.253, to whom may each licensee disclose confidential information about their respective client?
choice_a: Any other licensee affiliated with the brokerage
choice_b: Only the real estate broker
choice_c: The Real Estate Division upon request
choice_d: The opposing party's attorney only
explanation: NRS 645.253(1) provides that each licensee assigned to separate parties 'shall not disclose, except to the real estate broker, confidential information relating to a client' in violation of NRS 645.254.

question: Which Nevada statute requires the Real Estate Division to regularly inspect the transaction files, trust records, and pertinent real estate business accounts of all real estate brokers and owner-developers?
explanation: NRS 645.195(1) states: 'The Division shall regularly inspect the transaction files, trust records and pertinent real estate business accounts of all real estate brokers and owner-developers to ensure compliance with the provisions of this chapter.'

question: Under NAC 645.655, where must a broker's complete transaction and trust account records be kept, and when must they be made available to the Division?
choice_a: Kept anywhere the broker chooses, available only by court subpoena
choice_b: Kept at the broker's home address only
choice_c: Kept only in electronic format outside the state for cybersecurity purposes
choice_d: Kept in Nevada and open to inspection and audit by the Division during its usual business hours, as well as other hours during which the licensee regularly conducts business
explanation: NAC 645.655(2) requires a complete record of each transaction, together with NRS 645.310 trust records, to be kept in Nevada and open to inspection and audit by the Division upon request during usual business hours and other hours the licensee regularly conducts business.

question: If a broker's required records are stored electronically, what does NAC 645.655(3) require when the Division requests to inspect or audit those records?
choice_a: Access to the computer or other equipment used to store the information must be made available to the Division
choice_b: The broker must print and mail paper copies within 30 days
choice_c: The broker must convert the records to a Division-approved format at the broker's own expense before the audit
choice_d: Nothing additional is required for electronic records
explanation: NAC 645.655(3) requires that if records the Division requests are stored electronically, access to a computer or other equipment used to store the information must be made available to the Division for its inspection or audit.

question: Before a real estate broker may remove business records from their disclosed location, what does NAC 645.655(4) require?
choice_a: Written pre-approval from the Nevada Real Estate Commission
choice_b: Written notice to the Division of the exact record location, with a further notice of the new location delivered before the records are removed
choice_c: Nothing; a broker may relocate records without notifying the Division
choice_d: A 90-day waiting period after notifying affected clients
explanation: NAC 645.655(4) requires the broker to give written notice to the Division of the exact location of records and to not remove them until delivering notice of the new location.

question: Under NAC 645.655(1), how must each real estate transaction of a brokerage be recorded to permit an audit by a Division representative?
choice_a: Alphabetically by client last name only
choice_b: Grouped only by calendar year of closing
choice_c: Numbered consecutively or indexed to permit audit
choice_d: Recorded solely in the broker's personal appointment calendar
explanation: NAC 645.655(1) requires each real estate transaction of a brokerage to be 'numbered consecutively or indexed to permit audit by a representative of the Division.'

question: Under NRS 645.313, the Division may investigate and audit any of a broker's financial accounts, regardless of whether the account is a trust account, upon what showing?
choice_a: The broker charged a commission above the customary local rate
choice_b: The broker has fewer than two affiliated salespersons
choice_c: The broker's office lease has expired
choice_d: Reasonable cause to believe the broker is insolvent, is in a financial condition creating a substantial risk of insolvency, or the audit is otherwise reasonably necessary to enforce the chapter
explanation: NRS 645.313(1) allows the Division to audit any financial account related to a broker's business if it has reasonable cause to believe the broker is insolvent or at substantial risk of insolvency, or determines the audit is reasonably necessary to administer or enforce the chapter.

question: Under NRS 645.314, the Administrator may charge a broker for the actual costs and fees of a Division audit under which circumstance?
choice_a: The broker fails, within a reasonable time, to comply with a Division request to produce or grant access to documentation required under NRS 645.310, where the Division has reasonable cause tied to a possible disciplinary matter
choice_b: The broker requests a copy of the audit report after completion
choice_c: The broker voluntarily submits to a routine annual inspection
choice_d: The broker hires outside counsel to represent the brokerage
explanation: NRS 645.314(1) permits charging audit costs and fees when the Division requests documentation the broker must maintain under NRS 645.310, the broker fails to comply within a reasonable time, and the Division has reasonable cause to believe the documentation would assist in investigating a disciplinable act.

question: Under NRS 645.314(2), within how many days must a broker pay a Division bill for audit costs and fees, and what penalty applies for late payment?
choice_a: 30 days; a flat $500 penalty
choice_b: 90 days; a 10 percent penalty plus an additional 1 percent for each month, or portion of a month, the bill remains unpaid
choice_c: 60 days; a 5 percent penalty only
choice_d: 180 days; no penalty applies
explanation: NRS 645.314(2) requires payment within 90 days after the broker receives the bill, with a late payment incurring a 10 percent penalty plus an additional 1 percent per month or partial month unpaid (waivable by the Administrator for good cause).

question: Under NRS 645.310(4), when a broker receives money belonging to others, into what type of account must it promptly be deposited?
choice_a: The broker's personal checking account, clearly labeled
choice_b: Any interest-bearing account chosen by the client
choice_c: A separate checking account located in a bank or credit union in Nevada that is designated a trust account
choice_d: A joint account held with the Real Estate Division
explanation: NRS 645.310(4) requires a broker who receives money belonging to others to promptly deposit it in a separate checking account at a Nevada bank or credit union designated as a trust account; the broker remains personally responsible and liable for the deposit at all times.

question: NRS 645.310(3) directly prohibits a real estate broker from doing what?
choice_a: Depositing earnest money before closing
choice_b: Accepting cash deposits from buyers
choice_c: Holding more than one trust account
choice_d: Commingling the money or other property of a client with the broker's own
explanation: NRS 645.310(3) states plainly: 'A real estate broker shall not commingle the money or other property of a client with his or her own.'

question: Under NRS 645.310(5), how often must a broker balance a separate trust account, and what must be provided to the Division annually?
choice_a: At least monthly; an annual accounting showing an annual reconciliation of each separate trust account, on a form provided by the Division
choice_b: Weekly; a list of all active listings
choice_c: Quarterly; a copy of the broker's tax return
choice_d: Annually; a notarized letter from the bank
explanation: NRS 645.310(5) requires the broker to balance each separate trust account at least monthly and to provide the Division, on a form it supplies, an annual accounting showing an annual reconciliation of each separate trust account.

question: Under NRS 645.310(6), what must each real estate broker notify the Division of regarding trust accounts?
choice_a: The routing number of the broker's personal bank account
choice_b: The names of the banks and credit unions where the broker maintains trust accounts, and the names of the accounts
choice_c: The Social Security numbers of all account signatories
choice_d: Nothing; trust account banking details are confidential from the Division
explanation: NRS 645.310(6) requires each broker to notify the Division of the names of the banks and credit unions in which trust accounts are maintained and to specify the names of the accounts on Division-provided forms.

question: Under NRS 645.310(7), if a broker holding trust account money dies or becomes mentally disabled, what may the Division do?
choice_a: Immediately seize and forfeit the funds to the State
choice_b: Automatically transfer the funds to the broker's next of kin
choice_c: Apply to the district court to have a trustee appointed to administer and distribute the money in the account, with court approval; the trustee may serve without posting a bond
choice_d: Void all pending transactions associated with the trust account
explanation: NRS 645.310(7) provides that upon a broker's death or mental disability, the Division may apply to the district court to have a trustee appointed to administer and distribute the trust account money with court approval, and the trustee may serve without posting a bond.

question: Under NAC 645.655(5), whose signature is required to withdraw money from a custodial or trust account, and what does not satisfy this requirement?
choice_a: Any office employee's signature; a typed name is acceptable
choice_b: The client's signature only; the broker's signature is not required
choice_c: A notary's signature; the licensee's own signature is optional
choice_d: A licensee's actual signature; a signature applied by use of a rubber stamp does not constitute the signature of a licensee
explanation: NAC 645.655(5) prohibits withdrawals without a licensee's signature and expressly states that 'a signature applied by use of a rubber stamp does not constitute the signature of a licensee' for this purpose.

question: Under NAC 645.655(6), may a real estate salesperson be the only required signatory on a custodial or trust fund account?
choice_a: No, a salesperson may not be the only required signatory but may be a cosigner with his or her broker
choice_b: Yes, provided the salesperson has at least two years of experience
choice_c: Yes, if the broker authorizes it in writing
choice_d: No, salespersons are barred from being any type of signatory on such accounts
explanation: NAC 645.655(6) states a real estate salesperson may not be the only required signatory on a custodial or trust fund account, but may be a cosigner on an account with his or her real estate broker.

question: Under NAC 645.655(7), if a real estate broker files for relief under federal bankruptcy law, what must the broker do with each trust account established under NRS 645.310?
choice_a: Freeze the account until the bankruptcy is discharged
choice_b: Immediately terminate the trust account and deposit all of its money into escrow, with executed instructions to disburse it under the original deposit agreement
choice_c: Transfer the funds to the Real Estate Division for safekeeping
choice_d: Convert the trust account into a general business account
explanation: NAC 645.655(7) requires a broker who files for bankruptcy relief to immediately terminate each NRS 645.310 trust account and deposit the money into escrow with executed instructions to the escrow agent to disburse it per the original deposit agreement.

question: Under NAC 645.655(8), what trust account structure must a broker who is engaged in property management maintain?
choice_a: A single combined trust account covering all rental operations and security deposits
choice_b: One trust account per client, regardless of the number of units managed
choice_c: Two separate property management trust accounts — one used solely for rental operations and one used solely for security deposits — plus a ledger account for each unit managed
choice_d: No separate trust account is required for property management funds
explanation: NAC 645.655(8) requires a broker engaged in property management to maintain two separate property management trust accounts (one for rental operations, one for security deposits), distinct from any other real estate trust account, plus a ledger account for each managed unit.

question: Under NAC 645.655(9), within how many days after receipt of the bank statement must property management and real estate transaction trust accounts be reconciled, and what deficit condition can trigger discipline?
choice_a: 10 days; any deficit at all triggers automatic license revocation
choice_b: 60 days; only deficits exceeding $10,000 are disciplinable
choice_c: There is no reconciliation deadline; only annual audits matter
choice_d: 30 days; a trust or ledger account left in deficit for more than 45 consecutive days in one year is subject to discipline under NRS 645.633(1)(h)
explanation: NAC 645.655(9) requires monthly reconciliation within 30 days after receipt of the bank statement, and a broker who permits a trust or ledger account to remain in deficit for more than 45 consecutive days in a year is subject to discipline under NRS 645.633(1)(h) or other applicable charges.

question: Under NAC 645.670, a Division inspection of a real estate office must include, at minimum, which of the following?
choice_a: The procedure used to deposit money, the trust records, and the indexing or numbering system used in filing records, among other items
choice_b: Only the broker's personal financial statements
choice_c: The broker's personal credit score
choice_d: A review of the broker's home mortgage
explanation: NAC 645.670(2) lists the required elements of a Division inspection, including the deposit procedure, trust records, and the filing indexing/numbering system, along with office signage, advertising, and availability of current statutes and regulations.
